notice: Authoring specifications only. These records do not register geography, spawn actors, add models or implement missions. Native owners and acceptance evidence are named for local implementation.

districts.name: Lantern Ward
districts.premise: A working harbor neighborhood tends the lamps of a convoy that never came home; its residents also need breakfast, coolant and a way through the afternoon traffic.
districts.geometry: A crescent of inhabited hulls around the existing Memorial Array, one public promenade route, an outside freight bypass and a narrow service cut. Keep the training claim and its departure corridor clear. The empty cradle is readable from all three routes.
districts.arrival: A lamp-lighter pulls alongside a dark berth while a passenger shuttle yields to a slow memorial tow. A repair arm works on a damaged shutter. The player sees who is waiting for whom before any job is offered.

landmark.name: The Empty Plinth
landmark.change: Retain the canonical memorial; build an inhabited crescent and a tow cradle around it. The missing lamp belongs to a living family, not a new unexploded-bomb story. The serviced family lamp and cradle are an adjoining new object; the Candle Fleet's canonical dark twenty-fifth memorial plinth remains dark and keeps its identity.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Finite lamp service cells supplied by an ordinary freight delivery; no cosmetic source creates stock.
Physical repair parts reserved once for an attended repair.
Durable service state of the affected lamp/berth, not a second commodity.

visibleSteps: Collect one cell at the freight platform.
Travel the public service loop with visible cargo.
Clamp at the adjoining family lamp, never the canonical dark twenty-fifth plinth; articulated service and a visible crew worker follow the actual native work phase.
Consume the cell only on confirmed service, light that lamp, return.
routines.interruption: Threat pauses service and causes retreat with the same cell. A destroyed lamp cannot be lit by a timer.
routines.recovery: Recover the same cell or obtain a new paid delivery; damaged mount needs repair.

visibleSteps: Open the passenger gate at its actual berth.
Wait while the slow tow crosses.
Depart along the promenade to the other dock.
Return on the next calendar shift, with stop lights and dwell.
routines.interruption: An obstructed lane yields or takes the signed bypass; passengers never unload into empty space.
routines.recovery: Physical obstruction removal reopens the normal route.

visibleSteps: Fetch a part.
Brace beside the real damaged shutter.
Work while attached; show arm contact and sparks only during service.
Leave a visibly restored shutter and a service receipt.
routines.interruption: Unlatching interrupts progress. Damage creates salvage once; no repair-from-distance.
routines.recovery: Retain damage and consumed-stock history across departure and Continue.

opportunities.title: The Empty Plinth
approaches: Escort the family tow to the empty cradle during ordinary traffic.
Borrow the tow cradle and move the disabled lamp yourself.
Clear the service cut so the crew can finish without you.
opportunities.commitReceipt: The exact lamp is secured at the matching cradle with its native service state restored; one local remembrance unlocks.
opportunities.failure: A broken lamp becomes a repair/recovery task. Missing the procession does not erase the family or restart time.
opportunities.revisit: The light is on, the family tow has a new berth and a shuttle now uses the reopened route.

opportunities.title: Five Minutes Late
approaches: Move the fallen traffic mast.
Escort the shuttle through the freight bypass.
Leave it alone and watch the tug resolve the obstruction later.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Actual shuttle arrival releases its existing schedule; no money for merely entering the area.
opportunities.failure: Causing a collision earns a witnessed liability and visible repair demand.
opportunities.revisit: Shuttle driver recognizes help or nuisance; the mast remains damaged until repaired.

opportunities.title: Borrowed, According to You
approaches: Ask the yard keeper for the portable tow cradle after helping.
Take the unclamped cradle during shift change and accept local theft consequences.
Buy the released surplus cradle when its work is complete.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Ownership/custody changes through the native object and crime owners; no cloned inventory reward.
opportunities.failure: A failed theft becomes retrieval or restitution rather than a reload.
opportunities.revisit: Your stored cradle remains the same object; its original berth is empty or supplied with a visibly delivered replacement.

assets.brief: Rearrange into a crescent with readable doors and clear flight gaps.
Use real arrival/service sockets.
Open two-prong cradle with lamp retention socket, powered/empty/damaged states; see asset bible.

acceptance.action: Watch a whole lamp-service and shuttle cycle without accepting a mission.
acceptance.expected: A real source, journey, wait and service result are visible. The serviced object is the family lamp; the original dark twenty-fifth memorial plinth remains dark.
acceptance.negative: Do not count a looping orbit or lamp timer.

acceptance.action: Break one lamp, leave, save/Continue and return; then repair it.
acceptance.expected: Damage persists, same service outcome changes only after real work.
acceptance.negative: Repeated load or repair event cannot duplicate parts or payouts.

districts.name: Niner Bastion
districts.premise: Gate 3 is a public crossing wrapped in an old fortress. The customs staff keep trade moving; the garrison keeps a more powerful machine behind the fence.
districts.geometry: Three nested bands: signed public approach, inspection aprons, restricted hangar court. Two maintenance side cuts and a convoy-sized front mouth. Cranes and shield pylons make cover; a rail of hulls makes the standing army legible before it attacks.
districts.arrival: Two pickets exchange watch, a mechanic opens COUNTERSIGN's clamp arms, an inspected convoy leaves, and a recruit practices stopping a ballast target. The restricted court is unmistakable but visibly penetrable.

landmark.name: Gate 3 and its sleeping Auditor
landmark.change: Retain Gate 3/weir owners and Lane Customs anchors. Niner is the surrounding yard. The existing Lane Relay POI remains a separate service object, not Gate 3 renamed. Do not turn the public trade lane into compulsory combat.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Finite repair/fuel inventory for grounded and returning garrison hulls.
Persistent roster identities: ready, on-duty, disabled, captured, lost or replenishing.
Local sensor/relay service state; this does not directly own global WANTED heat.

visibleSteps: Relief pair leaves a named berth.
Old watch transfers inspection duty at the marked gate.
Returning pair enters the repair lane.
Mechanic services the same hulls before they rejoin reserve.
routines.interruption: A witnessed intrusion commits only the available responders; civilians clear the firing lane.
routines.recovery: Damaged units limp back; lost units stay lost until a finite supply-backed replacement arrives.

visibleSteps: Service crane opens.
Crew transfers a physical spare/fuel pod.
COUNTERSIGN cycles a cargo clamp on a marked ballast target.
Tender rests at the same berth.
routines.interruption: Stolen fuel or severed power delays readiness; service animation must stop when its owner cannot work.
routines.recovery: Restore supply or recover the hull; no timer manufactures a second COUNTERSIGN.

visibleSteps: Queue before the visible scan beam.
Hale/Dree challenge a target with a local reason.
Approved hulls cross the actual opening.
A stopped hull is escorted to inspection, leaving space for the next.
routines.interruption: Warnings name who is challenged and why; a warning is not already an attack.
routines.recovery: Leaving the restricted band or complying clears the local challenge; global legal consequences stay with law.

opportunities.title: Borrowed Authority
approaches: Enter as a legitimate maintenance contractor and board the unoccupied tender.
Break the relay, slip through the service cut and disable the berth clamp.
Go loud: dismantle the screening formation and escape through the freight mouth.
opportunities.commitReceipt: BLACK FLAG transfers control of the same disabled/unoccupied COUNTERSIGN generation; old player hull and cargo retain custody.
opportunities.failure: A jammed transfer keeps the old player hull controllable; losing the tender leaves a recoverable wreck or impound, not a fabricated success.
opportunities.revisit: The original hangar is empty, the garrison logs a specific loss and your tender retains its serial and damage.

opportunities.title: Target Practice, Revised
approaches: Pull the training ballast into a different lane to distract the watch.
Win a sanctioned live-physics drill and earn access.
Use the ballast as cover during a heist.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Real target motion affects the actual watch/drill result; no score for pressing an interaction button.
opportunities.failure: Injured friendlies produce proportional witnessed consequences; no faction-wide omniscience.
opportunities.revisit: Bent targets, a postponed drill or a grudging invitation remain.

opportunities.title: The Last Bus Through
approaches: Escort a civilian shuttle during an alarm.
Restore the public relay after sabotaging it.
Negotiate a short corridor using physical evidence of the shuttle's cargo.
opportunities.commitReceipt: The identified shuttle clears the gate with its manifest; local outcome is independent of heist completion.
opportunities.failure: Missed departure moves passengers to a real refuge with another route; never locks the campaign graph.
opportunities.revisit: A refugee berth fills or empties and the driver remembers what actually happened.

assets.brief: Build the public apron and clear stopping marks.
Readable connected sensor line; no unexplained invisible boundary.
Warden/repair-tender derivative with two cargo clamp arms, one short-lived screening field and an exposed service socket; not a generic damage upgrade.
Open-front armored hangar court, roof panels split for camera visibility, two side cuts and visible reserve berths.

acceptance.action: Provoke two successive alarms, disable and capture defenders, leave and return.
acceptance.expected: Roster conservation, finite reinforcements and visible replacement work.
acceptance.negative: No spawn behind the camera or reset refill.

acceptance.action: Attempt transfer while destroyed, paused, replaced, out of range and while another transfer is pending.
acceptance.expected: Invalid attempts deny safely; valid transfer keeps exact hull identity and possessions.
acceptance.negative: No duplicated hull, cargo or dead-player control.

districts.name: The Switchyard
districts.premise: Meridian built a freight interchange; the people who could not afford to leave built a town in its disused sidings. The oldest routing machine still delivers to a neighborhood that has moved.
districts.geometry: A large freight spine with three side courts: exchange, domestic berths and unofficial transshipment. The Split Station remains two real physical halves. Public traffic loops around a narrow shunter crossing; service alleys connect courts without crossing every convoy.
districts.arrival: A shunter draws six coupled pods across the player's path; a lunch skiff slips under the stopped convoy's coupler, a school shuttle waits, and a repair drone paints a new address over an older one.

landmark.name: The Wrong Address
landmark.change: Use the existing split-station anomaly and its actors; add a domestic receiver that has physically moved. Do not clone the canonical station halves.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Native shipment lots with source, destination and custody.
Delivered household stock; receives only the appropriate finite lot.
Persistent switch and address destination, distinct from discovered-map position.

visibleSteps: Collect a finite train from the intake.
Signal and wait for the passenger crossing.
Pull it through the spine.
Detach the exact destination pod at the receiver; return with empties.
routines.interruption: Broken couplers leave actual pods; traffic routes around obstruction.
routines.recovery: An NPC or player can tow the same lot to a lawful receiver.

visibleSteps: Service lit domestic berths.
Dock at the canteen/clinic.
Wait during freight priority.
Return to a real endpoint on shift change.
routines.interruption: A closed service receiver postpones the run visibly; it does not secretly refill.
routines.recovery: Goods restoration resumes the next service occurrence.

visibleSteps: Read the old address on the physical shipment.
Carry it toward the vacated siding.
Wait at an absent receiver and request a correction.
Use the corrected receiver only after native destination change.
routines.interruption: Player seizure becomes custody; fake proximity at the new berth cannot transfer the load.
routines.recovery: Correct the address physically or redirect the same pod by towing; keep compensation with its owner.

opportunities.title: The Wrong Address
approaches: Tow the lost refrigerator pod to the inhabited half.
Move the receiver mast and register the legitimate destination.
Persuade the clerk with a recovered shipping plate, then accompany the corrected run.
opportunities.commitReceipt: The exact finite lot reaches the correct working receiver; a canonical destination receipt changes future deliveries.
opportunities.failure: Damaged cargo supplies fewer units; blocked route leaves an address dispute and physical recovery job.
opportunities.revisit: Clinic lights and household deliveries change; the sorter stops returning to empty space.

opportunities.title: No Such Thing
approaches: Fund one real canteen shipment.
Escort a delayed produce load.
Steal it and sell through the Quiet Cache, accepting a visible shortage.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Only actual delivered quantity changes canteen stock and native payment.
opportunities.failure: Lost goods become salvage or shortage; no arbitrary global famine from one lunch crate.
opportunities.revisit: The canteen opens a hatch, changes its queue or posts a specific shortage.

opportunities.title: The Switching Fee
approaches: Rent the impulse shunter.
Earn its use by clearing a derailment.
Hijack it and improvise a moving barricade.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Control/tool access comes through native vehicle/service authority with actual mass and coupling limits.
opportunities.failure: Overweight consists do not move by script; an escape route remains.
opportunities.revisit: Bent couplers and abandoned pods persist until a crew resolves them.

assets.brief: Domestic courts with visible sheltered queues and shutter states.
Physical goods handoff with contact/empty/loaded articulation.
Branching rail/truss kit whose geometry shows freight priority and pedestrian habitation; named junction sockets.
Low wide tow body; two visible couplers; forward impulse shoe, no decorative train teleportation.

acceptance.action: Steal, spill, recover and deliver the same marked lot.
acceptance.expected: Conserved quantity, one owner and one payout.
acceptance.negative: A bare delivery event or replacement entity never grants stock.

acceptance.action: Fly in by two different entrances without the map open.
acceptance.expected: The freight spine and three distinct courts give a navigable mental map.
acceptance.negative: More random station kit scatter does not satisfy composition.

districts.name: The Cathedral
districts.premise: Sixty years of extraction turned an ore body into a neighborhood of vaults. Its people know the rock by the notes its supports make under load.
districts.geometry: A very large connected hollow rock adjacent to the saved Wreck Cathedral site: three shipping mouths, six narrow service mouths, two chambers connected by an extraction nave and a shorter dangerous side passage. Retain the existing Wreck Cathedral geometry and ID as a nearby grave, not the rock shell.
districts.arrival: The rock occludes the sky. An ore tug emerges from a lit mouth with a line taut behind it; a cutter stops while a crew shuttle crosses the nave. A suspended quarry bell shivers when the load train passes.

landmark.name: Nine-Mouth Cut
landmark.change: New neighboring mined rock; preserve the existing Wreck Cathedral object and saved workfleet. The district title describes both work and mourning, not an identity swap.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Finite native ore source and extraction product.
Load-bearing service state and exact installed brace identity.
Reserved passage capacity, not a reward counter.

visibleSteps: Brace at an actual seam.
Cut native ore into a real load.
Transfer to a tug only in range.
Move through a cleared mouth to the existing refinery.
routines.interruption: Danger shuts the cutter down and leaves its load; supply cannot appear in the receiver.
routines.recovery: Recover or recut from remaining source; respect depleted field records.

visibleSteps: Visit each physical brace.
Strike the quarry bell/structure to test it.
Mark a damaged member.
Return with a replacement and install while attached.
routines.interruption: A collapse changes navigable geometry; no camera mode lets a ship fly through the blocked route.
routines.recovery: Alternate public mouth stays usable; physical shoring opens the shorter route.

visibleSteps: Wait at a lit entrance.
Request the single-lane passage.
Cross the actual nave in view.
Release the reservation at the exit.
routines.interruption: Player mass or debris obstruction makes it stop early rather than interpenetrate.
routines.recovery: Reverse to a passing bay; a route timeout returns the same passengers home.

opportunities.title: The Ninth Mouth
approaches: Tow a replacement brace into place before moving the jammed load.
Use the long safe shipping mouth to evacuate the crew.
Exploit a timed cutting pause to take the narrow service route with a light hull.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Exact brace installation and/or identified evacuee arrival change the opening state; extraction profit is separate.
opportunities.failure: A jam or collapse strands recoverable cargo and reroutes work; no softlock or forced civilian death.
opportunities.revisit: The supported mouth reopens, or permanent rubble changes the route while repair crews keep working.

opportunities.title: What the Rock Can Carry
approaches: Sound the resonator to locate a stressed member.
Unload the overweight tug.
Bring in a heavier anchor and share the load with a physical rig.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Native load/contact evidence controls the intervention; no dialogue choice solves a mechanical failure.
opportunities.failure: A wrong pull breaks a replaceable member and moves the evacuation window.
opportunities.revisit: A named brace carries your patch and the inspector's route changes.

opportunities.title: The Portable Mountain
approaches: Borrow the quarry winch after a service run.
Buy a retired head.
Recover a dropped winch from an unsafe side chamber.
opportunities.commitReceipt: The same usable winch head enters custody or installs on a valid mount.
opportunities.failure: A lost head can be recovered; it is not awarded again on revisiting.
opportunities.revisit: The borrowed machine's absence changes a crew's available lift until returned.

assets.brief: Use for extraction nave with meaningful load sockets.
Chunked traversable rock shell with explicit holes and swept collider clearance; distant body plus real local panels.
Pendulous resonator with clear swing constraints, strike face and strain response.

acceptance.action: Enter, reverse, tow a wider load, save mid-tunnel and Continue.
acceptance.expected: Stable reference frame, visible exit, unchanged physical collision and restored load.
acceptance.negative: Camera cannot pass through roofs or make blocked openings traversable.

acceptance.action: Run the route in nonzero-origin Ceres and after an origin rebase.
acceptance.expected: Objects, HUD route and colliders coincide.

districts.name: Widow's Run
districts.premise: A wreck gauntlet conceals Quiet Berths, a town whose households live in ships declared destroyed. Some residents smuggle medicine; some smuggle people who would rather not be cargo.
districts.geometry: Three connected wreck throats: a broad licensed lane, a tug-width hull corridor and a short dark coupler alley. The quiet court lies beyond the second bend. A massive freighter prow and an upside-down garden window orient the player. Choke points contain passing bays and retreat space.
districts.arrival: Two tugs maneuver a dead hull in a funeral procession while another crew strips its outer plates. Children's lit windows remain visible inside the procession hull. A sentry waves familiar traffic through without treating every smuggler as hostile.

landmark.name: The Never-Landed Ferry
landmark.change: Compose around the saved wreck/Quiet nodes; a inhabited ferry shell is proposed adjacent scenery with real service berths and legal custody distinctions.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Finite salvage lots held by real crews.
Known shipment whose receiver is the clinic, not a generic credit sink.
Route obstruction, opened coupler and local trust states.

visibleSteps: Latch the same inhabited ferry hull.
Wait for the cutter to stop in the shared throat.
Tow to the memorial berth.
Unlatch and release the public lane.
routines.interruption: Attack scatters attendants into named shelters; the hull remains a real obstacle and rescue target.
routines.recovery: Return the lost hull or clear a different berth; remember casualties without erasing the town.

visibleSteps: Assess the existing wreck.
Cut a chosen recoverable piece.
Pass it to the yard tug.
Deliver to the foundry intake.
routines.interruption: Cutting a structural coupler changes the route; real collateral implicates the actual attacker.
routines.recovery: A crew can repair the service lane using finite purchased materials.

visibleSteps: Hide a marked pod in a hull alcove.
Observe an actual patrol crossing.
Move the same pod through the quiet lane.
Deliver at the clinic receiver.
routines.interruption: A patrol with no witness cannot magically know the hiding place.
routines.recovery: The runner waits, reroutes or asks for physical escort; no new duplicate pod.

opportunities.title: Funeral Freight
approaches: Help tow the ferry and protect its occupants.
Use the funeral as cover for a medical shipment.
Steal a valuable unoccupied engine while the crews are occupied.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Actual delivery/custody and occupied-hull safety outcomes independently settle.
opportunities.failure: A theft can become a rescue; rescue does not erase the theft, and one mistake does not permanently close all Quiet trade.
opportunities.revisit: A berth is inhabited, a clinic is stocked, or a family mourns at a specific damaged hull.

opportunities.title: A Short Cut Through Someone's Kitchen
approaches: Ask permission to use the family service gap.
Clear the blocked public route instead.
Blast through an occupied side passage and face the local repair claim.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Native passage opening changes the route and the affected home state.
opportunities.failure: Do not silently kill unseen families; occupied hazard must be visibly and audibly signaled before commitment.
opportunities.revisit: Windows, shutters, resident routes and toll/access change according to the action.

opportunities.title: Widowmaker, Secondhand
approaches: Recover a coupler ram from a stalled tug.
Buy a salvage lease and work it loose.
Hijack the tug then return or keep the rig.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Same-body rig custody; mass and clearance govern escape.
opportunities.failure: An oversized rig becomes stuck visibly and can be detached or recovered.
opportunities.revisit: Its seller, owner or bereaved crew recognizes the actual object later.

assets.brief: Irregular domestic berths in salvaged hull cavities.
Hidden-but-readable transshipment receiver.
Unmistakable ferry prow, warm patched interior courts, detachable exterior scrap and protected inhabited core.
Three distinct broken hull portals, passing alcoves and explicit load-width thresholds.

acceptance.action: Reach the clinic via fast, safe and concealed routes in two ship sizes.
acceptance.expected: Topology changes decisions and appropriate route access.
acceptance.negative: Routes cannot differ only by cosmetic color.

acceptance.action: Enter unarmed; help one crew, steal from another, leave and return.
acceptance.expected: Separate local memories and civil routines; no faction-wide instant war.
acceptance.negative: A neutral smuggler must not become an enemy solely because its faction is Quiet.

districts.name: Memorial Gardens
districts.premise: Gardeners turn wrecks into shelter and food at the edge of the Bloom. A filament can hold a greenhouse together or connect it to a predator; the same material does both.
districts.geometry: Three inhabited wreck hulls bridge across an open garden court. Safe pruned routes, a porous tissue tunnel and a bright hot machinery lane form different approaches. The growth surface fills the lower frame while native hull silhouettes still tell where the colony begins.
districts.arrival: A gardener cuts a mature filament and carries it to a greenhouse brace; a shepherd pulses and a line of harmless scavengers changes direction. Further out, a similar pulse draws predators toward hot machinery.

landmark.name: Greenwake
landmark.change: Develop the existing Three Hull Garden and Understory owners; do not register a parallel infestation ledger or consume the same wreck twice.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Canonical finite wreck mass, shared with salvage and nursery owners.
Existing persistent garden growth and service state.
Exact living shepherd/node identity and bounded pulse state.

visibleSteps: Inspect the real wreck for occupants.
Tow accepted scrap to the living receiver.
Feed only material held in valid custody.
Prune the grown branch and carry its usable product home.
routines.interruption: A player may rescue the hull or divert it; occupied hulls are never casually fed.
routines.recovery: Spoiled or missing source stays missing; new stock must arrive physically.

visibleSteps: Inspect the corridor membrane.
Cut one hazardous bridge with a readable tool.
Wait for scavengers to pass.
Deposit pruned biomass at the greenhouse.
routines.interruption: Cutting the wrong bridge closes shelter as well as a predator path.
routines.recovery: Install a real brace or regrow the safe connection using existing ecology rules.

visibleSteps: Pulse with a visible leading cue and non-flashing mode.
Creatures within the native radius react by species.
Attendant stays outside the dangerous route.
Pulse has a quiet refractory period.
routines.interruption: Harvesting the organ disables this actual node; it cannot also keep pulsing as scenery.
routines.recovery: Rescue or reinstall the same organ, or let the garden adapt to its absence.

opportunities.title: Green Debt
approaches: Quarantine the hot wreck and protect the greenhouse.
Tow the wreck to a safe feed mouth after rescuing its occupant.
Sever the spreading bridge and rebuild the greenhouse support mechanically.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Canonical rescue, consumed wreck mass and garden stage produce separate durable results; no moral option overwrites physics.
opportunities.failure: A failed cut spreads danger into one readable route; evacuation and repair remain possible.
opportunities.revisit: The route is pruned, scarred, regrown or reinforced, and the gardener's work changes.

opportunities.title: Second Skin
approaches: Grow a protective membrane from delivered material.
Use a metal shield rig instead.
Sell the biomass and accept a short-term shelter shortage.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Physical installed protection responds to actual impacts and native damage.
opportunities.failure: Lost shelter alters convoy behavior without making a whole region unusable.
opportunities.revisit: A patched greenhouse changes silhouette and its repair crew stops repeating the completed work.

opportunities.title: Borrow a Voice
approaches: Earn a harvested pulse organ after helping the attendant.
Take the live organ and face ecological consequences.
Rescue one from a dead node before it decays.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Unique organ custody and usable pulse with native cooldown/affected-species rules.
opportunities.failure: An unsafe pulse can attract a threat; it does not always conveniently stun every enemy.
opportunities.revisit: The former site grows differently and the stolen organ is recognized.

assets.brief: Retain steel windows and doors under growth so scale stays readable.
Cuttable membrane spans with anchor roots, five persistent stage variants, clear positive/negative space.
Warm occupied greenhouse court grafted into a broken cargo hull; repair sockets and emergency shutters.

acceptance.action: Feed, sell, destroy and reload a marked wreck in competing orders.
acceptance.expected: Exactly one custody settlement and no duplicated material.
acceptance.negative: Event strings alone cannot claim consumption.

acceptance.action: Prune one bridge, save, return through its old line, then restore another.
acceptance.expected: Ecology, collision, navigation and visual growth agree.
acceptance.negative: A green decal with unchanged routes is insufficient.

districts.name: The Iron Maw
districts.premise: An industrial dreadnought shell has accreted around the dead Deep-Mother. Its administrative beacon still orders a shift change, and people living in the keel have learned to steal power from the dead war.
districts.geometry: Layered but physically XZ navigable surface districts: radiator plain, gun trench, relief court, machinery throat and vault interior. The hull fills the visible ground below the ship. Horizons and macro silhouette imply a larger body; reachable panels have real colliders and joints. No single solid sphere under an enterable hole.
districts.arrival: The starfield disappears behind panelwork. A headlight sweeps grooves under the ship. Maintenance tugs crawl between dead batteries; an inhabited court opens warm shutters while an obsolete gun tries to track a harmless utility barge.

landmark.name: The Iron Maw / Dead Shift
landmark.change: Reconcile existing dead Deep-Mother boss and dreadnought prose by retaining the corpse/vault inside an accreted human hull shell. Existing killed/boss states remain authoritative; exterior construction is new proposed content.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Power route/service state committed by native machinery controls; no abstract player mana.
Finite coolant supply physically brought to relief infrastructure.
Persistent exact detachable hull plate/crane load with physical mass.

visibleSteps: Leave the relief court with a coolant pod.
Follow a radiator service trench.
Clamp at the failing pump.
Return with the empty pod as lights change in the served court.
routines.interruption: An exposed run can be intercepted; the barge stops work when the line breaks.
routines.recovery: Recover the same pod or deliver a replacement; no automatic restore on reentry.

visibleSteps: Lock the crane foot.
Lift a real detachable cover.
Wait for service craft to cross under it.
Lower and latch at the marked seat.
routines.interruption: A cut cable drops actual mass; emergency stop does not erase momentum.
routines.recovery: Winch or tow the same plate out of the route; secondary escape stays open.

visibleSteps: Scan a narrow visible arc.
Cue its windup.
Fire only on authorized target categories.
Cool and rotate, leaving a forecastable crossing window.
routines.interruption: Rerouting power changes the actual battery; residents notice loss of supply.
routines.recovery: Alternate routing or physical disable leaves a changed but traversable surface.

opportunities.title: The Last Relief
approaches: Keep the colony powered while removing the harmful control stack.
Evacuate the court, then use the crane and plates to dismantle the battery.
Bargain for access, physically isolate the vault and take evidence rather than destroy everything.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Separate native evacuation, power, boss and evidence receipts decide the result; no ending fires because a cutscene timer elapsed.
opportunities.failure: Failed evacuation leaves specific recoverable survivors; an already-dead boss never respawns to serve the new plot.
opportunities.revisit: The Gutted Maw has the actual missing panels, survivor settlement and usable routes you left.

opportunities.title: A Window in the Gun
approaches: Route a service cable through the gun's blind interval.
Rotate a dead panel into cover with the crane.
Follow a maintenance barge through the protected trench.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Actual traversal with load clears the task, using physical line of sight and geometry.
opportunities.failure: A hit drops repair cargo and makes recovery the new job.
opportunities.revisit: Your improvised panel shield remains a future navigation landmark.

opportunities.title: Surface Rights
approaches: Lease a working surface crane.
Take control after isolating its hostile owner.
Repair its controls and let the residents use it while you handle the load.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Native control lease and real moved plate; no click-to-remove wall.
opportunities.failure: Insufficient anchor load, broken tether or power loss denies motion truthfully.
opportunities.revisit: Residents use the reclaimed machine or complain about a missing one.

assets.brief: Local maintenance sockets and human scale cues.
Chunked steel terrain kit: macro ribs, walkable-by-ship trenches, radiator fields, detached panels; never a giant close-up texture plane.
Inhabited negative space in the keel with shutters, shelter, dock mouth and evacuation lanes.
Root, slew, boom, hook and brake sockets; collider follows native moving parts.

acceptance.action: Fly the radiator plain, enter the trench and emerge at the relief court.
acceptance.expected: Ground occupies the frame continuously; native panel silhouette, lighting and collider agree.
acceptance.negative: Enlarging a distant background object or changing sky color does not satisfy the place.

acceptance.action: Dismantle a plate, save mid-crisis and return after resolution.
acceptance.expected: No duplicate boss, plate, survivors or reward; world reflects the same causal outcome.
acceptance.negative: A generic intact model cannot silently replace the gutted body.

districts.name: Fourth Toll
districts.premise: Pilgrims leave bells for people they cannot bring home. The fourth toll is deliberately silent so crews on distant work shifts can answer it themselves.
districts.geometry: A low-density refuge organized around an open circle of resonators, an active repair berth and a weather-sheltered approach. Empty space is composed: the bells and light path keep bearing while long shadows allow quiet coasting.
districts.arrival: Three bells sound. On the fourth interval everyone waits. A distant repair ship answers with an engine pulse, then work resumes. A cook skiff carries a pot to a late crew. There is no immediate combat pop-up.

landmark.name: The Missing Fourth Bell
landmark.change: Develop the existing Echo Shrine zone using Struck Bell and BELLHOP/return hooks. The Shard Sphere POI keeps its identity as an adjacent landmark; do not rename it into a bell. The district adds social practice around existing owners rather than another duplicate bell quest.

population.admission: Planning envelopes, not raised runtime defaults. The current default shared budget is 24; any denser admission must coordinate existing owners and demonstrate cost. Reserve is finite logical inventory, not additional simultaneous bodies.

resources.description: Finite relief supplies for visiting damaged hulls.
Persistent arrangement/tuning of actual resonators.
Completed attended service on a specific visiting hull.

visibleSteps: Collect a resonator needing service.
Carry it along the lit approach.
Seat and tune it at a real socket.
Wait through the silent fourth interval before departure.
routines.interruption: A missing or damaged bell actually changes the sound/visual pattern.
routines.recovery: Use captions and visible motion to expose the same state for players who cannot hear it.

visibleSteps: Dock beside a damaged traveler.
Take a finite kit from the refuge receiver.
Remain attached while working.
Unlatch and let the repaired hull leave under native flight.
routines.interruption: Separation or danger stops repair; departure does not occur by pose teleport.
routines.recovery: If supply is stolen, traveler waits or gets towed to a second refuge.

visibleSteps: Leave the small canteen hatch.
Wait for the bell tow to pass.
Dock at the work berth.
Return after service.
routines.interruption: A collision spills a visible bounded prop lot, not an infinite loot source.
routines.recovery: A local apology, repair or replacement changes the next greeting.

opportunities.title: The Quiet Bell
approaches: Recover and tune the displaced resonator.
Carry a stranded crew into listening range.
Leave the missing fourth place empty at the family's request and repair the approach instead.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Native resonator/crew/approach outcomes remain distinct; a chosen silence is not an incomplete objective.
opportunities.failure: A broken resonator yields a salvage/rebuild route; never forces combat on a peaceful choice.
opportunities.revisit: The sound pattern, lights and waiting visitors reflect the actual choice.

opportunities.title: A Light They Can Find
approaches: Relight a safe approach with delivered cells.
Tow a repair ship through the unlit lane.
Install a rescued resonator as an alternate signal.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Actual arrival and service receipts; no reward for arbitrary dwell in a circle.
opportunities.failure: Failed rescue leaves a known distress contact and recoverable equipment.
opportunities.revisit: A named visitor returns; the beacon is useful to other ships as well as the player.

opportunities.title: The Bell You Carry
approaches: Earn a tuned resonator cluster for a service.
Salvage one from a dead pilgrimage barge.
Steal one and live with the missing voice at the shrine.
opportunities.commitReceipt: Same object custody grants a physics resonance capability with material-specific behavior.
opportunities.failure: Resonance cannot universally stun every material or bypass protection.
opportunities.revisit: The shrine audibly/visually lacks that cluster until a real replacement arrives.

assets.brief: Sheltered listening rooms and visible residents at ship-camera scale.
Sparse hanging bell court, one deliberately empty socket and modest lit refuge; repair and listening sockets remain clear.

acceptance.action: Spend one full shift here with no weapon use.
acceptance.expected: A legible routine, optional intervention and changed return state still exist.
acceptance.negative: Do not count text-only lore or mandatory attackers as activity.

acceptance.action: Play bell task muted and with reduced flash/motion.
acceptance.expected: Equivalent timing and action cues remain visible without revealing hidden outcomes.
acceptance.negative: No audio-only completion clue or compulsory camera motion.
